newsitem.title: USA: Ohio air traffic control regains lost power.
newsitem.headline: Ohio air traffic control regains lost power.

text.p: Communications and radar systems at an Ohio air traffic control center were nearly fully restored on Sunday after an unexplained loss of power created flight delays and some anxious moments on Saturday.

A spokesman for the Federal Aviation Administration's Great Lakes Center said the Oberlin, Ohio, control center, which tracks planes travelling over six states from New York to Indiana, was working with most of its systems operational.

The one hour, seven minute outage that began at 4:20 p.m. EDT (2020 GMT) on Saturday left controllers at the Air Route Traffic Control Center 30 miles (50 km) southwest of Cleveland peering at faded radar screens and scrambling to determine whether some 180 planes in the air were on a collision course.
"We were really sweating it out watching weak images on the screens, trying to determine if any were on converging flight paths," a controller said.

Roughly 75 percent of the flights scheduled to leave airports in Cleveland, Pittsburgh and Detroit were delayed up to two hours late Saturday afternoon by the outage, airport authorities said. A backup power source for the 18-month-old system at the control center also failed.

The FAA said it did not know the source of the problem. Various breakdowns over the past few years have plagued other air traffic control centers across the United States, as the FAA replaces aging equipment.
